bihar_raw_news.title: After Jamui, now molestation cases in 2 more Bihar districts - The Navhind Times
bihar_raw_news.content: SHARE Patna: Days after the horrific molestation case in Bihar’s Jamui district, a girl was allegedly harassed in public by a group of people in Samastipur and a minor was “sexually assaulted” in Muzaffarpur, prompting the Opposition to target the BJP-led NDA government over the law and order situation. The fresh incidents led to the arrest of altogether five persons, police said on Thursday. In Samastipur, the police arrested four persons who have been booked under relevant sections of the BNS, besides the IT Act and POCSO Act, after a video went viral on social media in which they could be seen molesting the girl. According to a statement issued by Samastipur police, the video “appears about a week old” and the victim was “yet to be identified”, though a case was lodged under the aforementioned laws since “the girl looked like a minor and the matter was sensitive”. Three of the accused, Vikas Kumar, Rahul Kumar and Rambabu Sahni, were residents of Jagatsinghpur village, where the incident had taken place, while the fourth, Awadhesh Paswan, hailed from Bijaulia. In adjoining Muzaffarpur, police arrested one Lalit Kumar, who had allegedly molested and beaten up a girl in the Town police station area. According to the Muzaffarpur police, the accused appeared to be mentally unstable, and his condition was being investigated by experts while the victim has been admitted to the Sadar Hospital for treatment. Police also debunked rumours on social media that a similar incident had taken place in Madhepura. According to the Madhepura police, a video that was being circulated was shot near a secondary school, and the students, male and female, were engaged in a heated debate after half-yearly examinations. The Madhepura police also said it will take action against “those who shared the video on social media with ulterior motives”. Meanwhile, the fresh incidents led to fresh attacks on the state’s BJP-led government from Opposition leaders like RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav and Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor. Yadav, who is the leader of the Opposition in the state assembly, linked the worsening law and order with alleged criminal antecedents of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. He also shared a video of minister Ashok Choudhary, claiming that the outbursts of the senior JD(U) leader were “a clear signal of administrative chaos that engulfs Bihar”. Ashok Choudhary, whose daughter Shambhavi is, incidentally, the LJPRV MP from Samastipur, can be heard saying the incidents in Bihar should not be fretted about as crimes against women took place “in highly advanced countries like America and Japan”. bihar_raw_news.title: India Infrastructure Push: How Expressways, Vande Bharat Trains Cut Travel Time
bihar_raw_news.content: India’s Infrastructure Revolution 2026: Check Key Vande Bharat, Bullet Trains, Expressways, Tunnel Routes; Travel Time Reduced to Minutes By Jaisal Kaur Last Updated: Sep 25, 2026, 13:40 IST Bridges have massively improved connectivity across rivers and rough terrain. The Bhupen Hazarika Setu, also known as the Dhola-Sadiya Bridge, reduced travel between Rupai in Assam and Meka/Roing in Arunachal Pradesh from around six hours to one hour As per government data quoted in recent reports, the Delhi-Mumbai road journey is targeted to fall from 33 to 12 hours, while Delhi-Katra travel reduces from 14 to 6 hours. India’s broadening network of expressways, bridges, tunnels and faster trains is decreasing travel times across major routes. Projects charted to bypass geographical barriers, reduce detours and bolster rail speeds are putting several long-distance journeys within shorter travel spans. According to government data quoted in recent reports, the Delhi-Mumbai road journey is targeted to fall from about 33 hours to 12 hours, while Delhi-Katra travel is slated to reduce from 14 hours to six hours. Bridges reduce long journeys Bridges have massively improved connectivity across rivers and rough terrain. The Bhupen Hazarika Setu, also known as the Dhola-Sadiya Bridge, reduced travel between Rupai in Assam and Meka/Roing in Arunachal Pradesh from around six hours to one hour. The Bogibeel Bridge has lowered the travel time between Dhemaji and Dibrugarh to almost a day to around one to two hours. In Bihar, the Kosi Rail Mahasetu reduced the Nirmali-Saraigarh rail journey from about eight hours to 30 minutes, while cutting the rail distance from nearly 300 km to around 22 km. Tunnels bypass difficult terrain Mountain tunnels are also cutting down travel distances and offering more reliable connectivity. The 9.02-km Atal Tunnel bypasses the Rohtang Pass, cutting around 46 km from the route and saving approximately four to five hours. The Dr Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel has lowered the Jammu-Srinagar road distance by about 30 km and saves nearly two hours. The Banihal-Qazigund twin-tube tunnel saves around 1.5 hours, while the Sela Tunnel has reduced travel time on the Tezpur-Tawang route by more than an hour. Expressways shorten road journeys Access-controlled highways are causing major reductions on inter-city routes. The Delhi-Meerut Expressway has brought travel time down from around 2.5 hours to about 50 minutes. The Bengaluru-Mysuru route has dipped from nearly three hours to around 75 minutes. Moreover, the Delhi-Dehradun Economic Corridor has reduced journey time from more than six hours to about 2.5 hours. Meanwhile, the Delhi-Amritsar-Katra Expressway is aimed at reducing Delhi-Amritsar travel from eight hours to four hours, and Delhi-Katra travel from 14 hours to six hours. The Delhi-Mumbai Expressway is being constructed to bring the journey from roughly 33 hours to about 12 hours. Vande Bharat adds speed to rail travel Indian Railways is also reducing journey times by upgrading present services and launching faster trains. bihar_raw_news.title: Village infrastructure improved significantly, urban-rural gap narrowed in 12 years: PM Modi
bihar_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Photo |ANI India Village infrastructure improved significantly, urban-rural gap narrowed in 12 years: PM Modi Modi said the country had also witnessed greater self-reliance among women since his government came to power in 2014. TNIE online desk Updated: 25th Sep, 2026 at 10:47 AM Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said the gap between urban and rural India had narrowed significantly over the past 12 years, with village infrastructure witnessing substantial improvement. Interacting with participants of the ongoing 'Seva Yatra' motorcycle rally from Varanasi to Vadnagar, Modi said the country had also witnessed greater self-reliance among women since his government came to power in 2014. "Over the past 12 years, the gap between cities and villages in India has significantly narrowed. Today, infrastructure in villages has improved significantly," Modi said. He said efforts towards social reform and positive change should continue irrespective of electoral considerations and stressed the need to work beyond "vote bank politics". Two motorcycle rallies were flagged off on September 17, Modi's 76th birthday, from Vadnagar in Gujarat and Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh. The rallies, which are scheduled to conclude on October 7, are being held to mark 25 years of Modi's public service. Vadnagar, where Modi was born, and Varanasi, which he has represented in the Lok Sabha since 2014, are the two endpoints of the rallies. The rallies are passing through towns, districts and villages, taking the message of service to grassroots communities while bringing together youth participation, social welfare, cultural engagement and community mobilisation. Modi said Vadnagar had given him the values that shaped his life, while Kashi had added "countless colours of service" to those values. On Thursday, Modi had interacted with participants of the rally travelling from Vadnagar to Varanasi. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will interact with participants of Seva Yatra today via video conference, who are travelling from Varanasi in UP to Vadnagar in Gujarat under Seva Sankalp Abhiyan. The interaction with the Prime Minister will give the Seva Yatris a chance to share their experiences from the journey, which is intended to connect youth participation and community service across the locations covered by the teams. The Seva Yatra began on September 17 and is part of the wider ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ to highlight PM Modi’s 25 years of public life. The participants are travelling through towns, districts, talukas and villages, with the programme focusing on taking community service and public engagement activities to the grassroots. The journey is not limited to a motorcycle expedition but is designed to bring together service, communication, youth participation, social welfare, cultural connect and community mobilisation at different locations along the route. The two-way motorcycle yatras between Varanasi and Vadnagar involve young participants travelling across multiple states, districts and villages. During the journey, the Seva Yatris have engaged with local communities and participated in service-oriented activities. These include cleanliness drives and interactions with beneficiaries and residents, as well as activities at schools, hospitals, nursing homes, and other community locations. The journey is scheduled to continue until October 7. The Prime Minister yesterday interacted with participants of the Seva Yatra, travelling from Vadnagar to Varanasi and praised their ongoing journey as a significant step toward grassroots nation-building. During the interaction, Mr Modi asked the participants about their experiences on the road, their interactions with people and the new learnings they had gathered during the journey. Drawing from his own organisational background within the party, Mr Modi acknowledged the hardships participants face, including shifting weather conditions and changing locations. During the interaction, the Prime Minister connected with the travellers’ current experiences, noting that such cross-country yatras play a vital role in helping the younger generation understand the country’s diversity. The interaction placed emphasis on the idea that a yatra is not merely about travelling from one place to another, but about meeting people, understanding communities and translating the spirit of seva into action. The Prime Minister also connected the ongoing efforts of the Seva Yatris with the larger journey of nation-building towards Viksit Bharat 2047, highlighting the role of young people in taking this spirit of service to the grassroots.

national_raw_news.title: 15 mins ago | National 12 Make in India initiative completes 12 years
national_raw_news.content: Today marks 12 years of Make in India. It was on this day in 2014 that the initiative was launched with the ambition of becoming a global hub for manufacturing, design and innovation. The initiative has transformed India’s manufacturing landscape by expanding production, investment and capabilities across industries. Akashvani correspondent reports that over the years, Make in India has opened new opportunities for businesses and investors to participate in India’s manufacturing journey. The initiative has subsequently been expanded under Make in India 2.0. The initiative now focuses on 27 sectors, which include 15 in manufacturing and 12 in services. The initiative focused on facilitating investment, fostering innovation and developing world-class infrastructure. Guided by ‘Minimum Government, Maximum Governance’, it has also sought to modernise processes and policies. Under the initiative, India’s electronics production increased nearly sevenfold, from 1.9 lakh crore rupees in 2014-15 to over 13 lakh crore in 2025-26. Mobile-phone production rose approximately 33-fold, from 18 thousand crore to 6.27 lakh crore over the same period. During this period, Indian Railways manufactured nearly 55 thousand coaches over 2014-24, while average annual railway coach production rose from less than 3 thousand 300 during 2004-14 to over 5 thousand during 2014-24. Over 6 thousand 6 hundred Linke Hofmann Busch (LHB) coaches were manufactured in 2025-26. Further, under the Make in India initiative, the country’s indigenous defence production increased from 46 thousand 429 crore in 2014-15 to a record 1.78 lakh crore in Financial Year 2025-26, bringing production to nearly four times its 2014-15 level. The initiative now goes beyond producing more goods and focuses on building the skills, technology and capacity needed to make them in India.

national_raw_news.title: 31 mins ago | Regional News 52 4th edition of UP International Trade Show to begin in Greater Noida
national_raw_news.content: The fourth edition of the UP International Trade Show (UPITS) will begin today at the India Expo Centre and Mart in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh. Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will inaugurate the five-day event. The exhibition, themed ‘Ultimate Sourcing Begins Here’, will run until September 29th, connecting the state’s entrepreneurs, manufacturers and exporters directly with the global market. Briefing the media, Uttar Pradesh MSME Minister Bhupendra Chaudhary highlighted the objective of establishing Uttar Pradesh as a global sourcing hub. He said the state is home to over 96 lakh MSME units and stated that UPITS will provide them with new opportunities for market expansion, investment, exports and employment. Akashvani correspondent reports that the event is expected to witness participation of over 2,400 exhibitors, 1.5 lakh B2B buyers and more than 4.5 lakh general visitors. Over 550 international buyers from 85 countries are also expected to attend the event. Partner countries for this edition include Austria, Japan, Russia, Singapore, Belarus and Vietnam. Additionally, reflecting the prominent role of women in trade and industry, around 300 women representatives will actively participate in the event. The exhibition will showcase various industries and sectors, including agriculture, automobiles, defence, IT, health, tourism and renewable energy. A major highlight this year is the introduction of the ‘One District, One Cuisine’ initiative, which will be featured alongside the ‘One District, One Product’ scheme to present the state’s traditional culinary heritage to the world. Buyers and exhibitors can pre-schedule their B2B meetings through a dedicated UPITS app. The event will also feature knowledge sessions, fashion shows and cultural programmes.
